title: Current portal guide
text: # Current portal guide

title: Source and hosting
text:
## Source and hosting
The live portal is the OpenAI-hosted balwyn-gate-automation project, with a Cloudflare Worker backend, D1 database binding DB and R2 object storage binding BUCKET. The GitHub branch real-source-from-chatgpt contains a source copy. A GitHub change does not publish the live portal. PR #10 was already merged and closed on 19 September 2026 before this update began.

title: Opening a gate and six-second pulses
text:
## Opening a gate and six-second pulses
Use the gate's Remote open control for the Compass ACB-004 Pi integration. The gateway waits up to 15 seconds and accepts pulse acknowledgements from 300 to 10,000 milliseconds. The browser waits up to 20 seconds. Six-second acknowledgements are supported. There is exactly one request and no automatic retry. A pulse acknowledgement confirms the trigger only, not that the gate physically opened. Independent sensors are needed to confirm position. If a request times out, inspect the gate before retrying.

title: Active gates
text:
## Active gates
Tony Frizza Stadium Entry and Side Entry are the two active single swing gates. The remaining seven registered gates remain inactive, including the office double gates, staff car park gates and boom gates. Channel assignment does not activate an inactive gate.

title: Equipment settings
text:
## Equipment settings
Open System settings and unlock with the administrator settings password. Equipment configuration includes remote-open enablement, four Compass channel assignments, dashboard refresh from 5 to 60 seconds, announcement speed and volume. Save equipment settings applies the portal changes. The Pi address and secret are server-side DOOR_SERVICE_URL and DOOR_SERVICE_TOKEN; an optional DOOR_GATE_MAP supplies default channel assignments. No hardware connection is inferred from a saved mapping. The settings panel reports whether address and credential are configured.

title: Pi configuration export
text:
## Pi configuration export
Pi pulse duration (300–10,000 ms), four BCM GPIO pins, polarity, GPIO chip and mock/dry-run/hardware mode are saved for export only. Download Pi configuration exports a file for reviewed local installation. Saving the portal does not update the Pi. Existing Pi tokens and journal paths are preserved, not exported. The included Pi service supports this duration range with a default of 500 ms. Older onsite service versions may require updating before a longer pulse setting can be used.

title: Login and administrator password
text:
## Login and administrator password
Normal sign-in and the administrator settings unlock are separate. Only an administrator can unlock configuration for ten minutes. Lock settings ends the unlock early. The login page has a password-reset request link. It requests administrator assistance rather than automatically issuing a reset email. Google, Microsoft and email sign-in availability depends on runtime configuration. Never paste passwords or service tokens into the helper.

title: Profiles and access
text:
## Profiles and access
Use the user profile editor for display name, username, contact details and photo. Photos use the R2 storage binding. Roles remain enforced on the server: viewers can read, operators can issue permitted commands, administrators can change protected configuration after unlocking. Controller credentials are issued separately and are not login passwords.

title: Schedules, automation and controllers
text:
## Schedules, automation and controllers
Schedules and automation have dedicated pages and require the administrator unlock to change. Schedule data alone is not proof that a physical gate follows it. The sensor-equipped controller workflow uses polling, heartbeats, a command queue and acknowledgements. Offline, uncommissioned or unsafe controllers cannot be treated as working live devices. Compass one-way relay open is a separate workflow without position feedback.

title: Roger controller and magnetic lock
text:
## Roger controller and magnetic lock
The existing Roger F70/IPU36 motor configuration, force, travel limits, safety circuits, local auto-close and maglock release sequence are set at the installed controller. These parameters are not remotely rewritten by this portal. Consult the project's Compass wiring reference and the installed equipment documentation. The helper has no ability to actuate equipment or change safety settings.

title: School site layer and meeting points
text:
## School site layer and meeting points
The uploaded balwyn_site.json file is sentinel-layout/2 and contains 22 marked outdoor exits, two meeting points (School oval and Eastern meeting point), and a central shared path called PINCH. These are exit-reference IDs, not the nine gate-control IDs. Routes are advisory, unverified against the approved emergency plan, with distances approximately ±10%. No building interiors, accessible-route distinction or refuges are included. The interactive site reference shows recorded connections and distances, not actual path geometry. Previewing PINCH unavailable excludes routes through that shared path. If there is no recorded alternative, the display says so. The map is not a live evacuation instruction and does not operate gates, doors or projectors.

title: CCTV, guidance and emergencies
text:
## CCTV, guidance and emergencies
CCTV, PTZ tracking and projector guidance require the relevant plan and actual commissioned equipment. No camera feed, fire detection, projector broadcast or safe route is inferred from a demonstration. Fire and lockdown command results require controller confirmation. Follow the school's approved emergency plan and authorised staff instructions. The helper cannot select live evacuation routes or initiate emergency actions.

title: Knowledge helper
text:
## Knowledge helper
The software helper searches the bundled project guides and can use an AI provider to explain matching excerpts. Source excerpts remain available when no AI key is configured. Answers cannot operate gates or edit settings. If the guides do not establish an answer, the helper must say so. For Claude, set AI_PROVIDER=anthropic, store ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a server secret and optionally set ANTHROPIC_MODEL. For OpenAI, select AI_PROVIDER=openai with OPENAI_API_KEY and optionally OPENAI_MODEL. Deploy after changing server configuration. Never paste keys into the help chat. A configured key is not proof of a successful provider response; the panel says AI connected only after an answer succeeds. Questions, recent conversation, matching guide passages and limited non-secret context are sent to that provider only when configured. No account credentials, user profiles, footage or activity records are automatically included.

title: Classroom projection screen
text:
## Classroom projection screen
The classroom concept preview uses the new GuidanceProjection component. Its example is the uploaded site layer's Exit 12 → central crossing (70.9 m) → School oval (17.2 m), approximately 88.1 m in total. The first instruction is to leave by Exit 12; the screen also says to stay clear of the internal driveway. This is an outdoor recorded connection, not a verified route from a named classroom. The displayed demonstration label remains visible. No live incident, connected projector or safe route is claimed.

title: Pi deployment status and commissioning
text:
## Pi deployment status and commissioning
At the owner's update on 19 September 2026 no Pi is deployed. There is no existing service URL, issued token or decided relay mapping to recover. School IT must first establish an approved route from the cloud portal to a genuine reachable HTTPS origin. The origin must have a valid certificate, no embedded credentials, no extra path, query or fragment. Generate a private printable service token of at least 32 characters during deployment, and configure the same value as Pi DOOR_API_TOKEN and portal DOOR_SERVICE_TOKEN without placing it in chat or Git. Decide and verify the channel assignment against the actual wiring. Software tests and a published pulse fix do not prove physical gate operation. A witnessed six-second open command returning a valid 200 acknowledgement, plus onsite checks, is still required. The independent sensor-controller agent has its own controller credentials when that workflow is used.

title: Shared-path inspection note
text:
## Shared-path inspection note
The recorded shared path to the oval is 17.2 m. Many recorded routes converge there. Inspect the physical opening on site: the route data does not establish its width, whether it is a single fence opening, or its capacity. Do not infer a confirmed bottleneck or a hardware remedy from distance alone.

title: Dashboard and navigation
text:
## Dashboard and navigation
Use the left navigation to open Dashboard, Gates & booms, CCTV & zones, Emergency guidance, Gate schedules, Automation, Safety protocol, Access & users, Activity log, or System settings. On a phone use the menu button to reveal navigation. The dashboard shows the two active gates. The Magic Keys AI-head background is branding, not an indicator that an AI controller is connected. The help button remains available across the signed-in workspace.

title: Gate lights, offline status and position
text:
## Gate lights, offline status and position
A green gate light represents confirmed open position and red represents confirmed closed position only when independent position feedback is current. Inactive gates are grey. Unknown, uncommissioned, offline, pending or failed controller states must not be read as open or closed. Controller feedback older than 90 seconds is stale. The ACB-004 open-only pulse has no position sensors; a successful trigger does not turn its physical position into a verified fact.

title: Activity log and CSV export
text:
## Activity log and CSV export
Open Activity log to review operator requests, settings changes and controller acknowledgements. Use Export CSV to download the displayed activity records; the button is unavailable when the list is empty. An entry saying requested or queued is not a completed operation. Read the acknowledgement or failure and its time when investigating a fault. The helper does not read or send the activity records to the AI provider.

title: Editing a profile photo or name
text:
## Editing a profile photo or name
Open Access & users and use the profile editor to change your own display name, portal username, contact information, job title or profile photo. Save the profile after editing. Use the photo controls to upload or remove your image. Changing a display name does not grant a different access role or change the sign-in password. Managing another person's profile requires administrator authority and the settings unlock.

title: Plan upgrades and locked features
text:
## Plan upgrades and locked features
Gate Operations is the core plan. Camera and advanced emergency-guidance features require Magic Keys Advanced. A module switch, relay assignment or administrator password does not grant a plan upgrade. Use the upgrade enquiry in the locked feature or contact RJL. Upgrading the plan does not connect cameras or commission hardware automatically; those are separate installation tasks. The outdoor site reference remains an advisory reference.

title: CCTV and camera connections
text:
## CCTV and camera connections
Open CCTV & zones for the camera workspace or feature preview. Camera event verification is a module in System settings. No live footage is connected merely because this switch is enabled. Camera feeds and authorised endpoints need separate commissioning. The multi-screen scenes and sample cameras explain the concept; they are not live surveillance. The helper cannot see camera footage, identify people or detect incidents.

title: Gate schedules and automation rules
text:
## Gate schedules and automation rules
Open Gate schedules, unlock administrator settings, select the gate and edit its weekly operating times before saving. Open Automation for operating rules. Both changes need administrator authority and the settings password. A saved timetable or enabled rule is stored configuration, not evidence that the Pi or controller has executed it. Check the commissioned controller workflow and activity acknowledgement. Do not assume an overnight hold or an automatic release is supported without confirming the installed controller behaviour.

title: Remote-open troubleshooting
text:
## Remote-open troubleshooting
If Remote open says not configured, the HTTPS service endpoint, shared secret and relay assignment have not all been installed. If configuration is incomplete, have the administrator review the endpoint format, token and map without posting them into chat. If no verified pulse acknowledgement is received, the trigger may already have occurred: inspect locally before another request. Do not repeatedly press Open. A dry-run response is a simulation. Inactive gates are blocked; emergency priority can also block manual remote open. Viewer accounts cannot operate gates.

title: Administrator unlock and access troubleshooting
text:
## Administrator unlock and access troubleshooting
Sign in as an administrator, open System settings, then enter the separate administrator settings password. A normal portal sign-in does not unlock relay settings. The unlock lasts ten minutes and can be ended with Lock settings. If controls relock, unlock again. If access is denied, confirm the approved account and role with RJL; changing profile details cannot bypass approval. Forgot password on the login page requests administrator assistance and does not itself reset the password.

title: Voice announcements and refresh interval
text:
## Voice announcements and refresh interval
Administrator equipment settings include dashboard refresh from 5 to 60 seconds, announcement speed from 0.5 to 1.5 and volume from 0 to 1. Monitoring settings include Australian English announcements. Device volume, browser speech support and available voices affect playback. Muting voice does not change a gate. Refreshing the dashboard polls portal data and does not prove the physical controller is connected.

title: Controller credentials and relay commissioning
text:
## Controller credentials and relay commissioning
Access & users contains Separate controller commissioning for the sensor-equipped OPEN/CLOSE agent. An administrator can issue or rotate a credential and download its setup file once. That credential is not the portal login or Pi DOOR_API_TOKEN. Transfer it securely to the intended controller and verify heartbeats, safety and position inputs. Issued credentials alone do not mean a controller is online. Compass ACB-004 remote open is a separate integration; do not mix its token or status with this workflow.

title: Project files, backups and deployment
text:
## Project files, backups and deployment
The complete project export includes the app frontend, server API routes, database schema and migrations, controller agent, Pi service, tests, guides and deployment package. Runtime secret values, live D1 records and R2 uploads are not included in a source export. Store secrets separately. Applying a GitHub change alone does not publish the OpenAI-hosted site. The bundled help index is rebuilt with the hosted build so guide updates ship with the matching version.

title: Help chat, sources and privacy
text:
## Help chat, sources and privacy
The Magic Keys help panel supports questions, follow-ups, current-page context, suggested questions, guide search and source passages. New chat clears the conversation in this browser tab. Reloading the page clears it too; conversations are not saved to the portal database or browser storage. When AI is configured, the current question, up to six recent messages, matching guides, page name, account role, plan and a non-secret configuration summary are sent to the configured provider, Anthropic (Claude) or OpenAI, named in the help panel. The account email, profile, activity log, footage, passwords and secret configuration values are not automatically sent. OpenAI requests use store:false. Claude uses the Anthropic Messages API. Provider handling and retention follow the applicable provider data policy; neither setting guarantees zero retention. Never type secrets or personal records into chat. Without a connection, the helper displays matching guide text clearly labelled as a guide excerpt. It cannot repair or operate hardware, change settings or reset passwords.

title: Per-account roles and existing accounts
text:
## Per-account roles and existing accounts
Each approved account can be assigned viewer, operator or administrator. Google approval entries accept email|role; Microsoft entries accept tenant-id:object-id|role. Password accounts use PORTAL_ROLE and PORTAL_SECONDARY_ROLE. Existing unannotated accounts retain administrator access for compatibility; this does not mean that school staff have already been assigned lower-privilege roles. RJL must explicitly configure those assignments. Invalid or duplicate role entries fail closed. Changing or removing an assignment invalidates the affected signed-in session and pending password verification; sign in again. Viewer access can read, operator access can issue permitted gate commands, and administrator access can manage protected settings after password verification. The helper cannot assign a role.

title: Controller reporting versus field commissioning
text:
## Controller reporting versus field commissioning
Controller reporting indicates current received heartbeat data. The internal legacy commissioned flag records that an initial healthy heartbeat with a known position was received; it is not a field commissioning record. No gate movement is required to set that flag. Reserve field commissioning for witnessed open-and-auto-close and the required onsite checks and sign-off. Neither a heartbeat nor the dashboard counts certify that this has happened.

title: Detection trial and false-alarm performance
text:
## Detection trial and false-alarm performance
Site-specific detection and false-alarm performance established at the paid trial stage. The portal does not publish a validated detection accuracy or false-alarm rate for the school. Concept demonstrations do not establish real-camera performance and must not be described as a tested live detection service.

title: Missing recorded alternatives are not blocked physical exits
text:
## Missing recorded alternatives are not blocked physical exits
When the shared path is excluded, 17 of the 22 exits have no recorded alternative in the supplied outdoor layer. This is a limitation of the traced data, not evidence that those exits are physically stranded or that no other route exists. The layer contains the routes drawn in the supplied overlay. Inspect and measure the opening and have the school verify routes before presenting any bottleneck finding or proposing a hardware remedy.

title: Owner access and restricted school accounts
text:
## Owner access and restricted school accounts
A server-configured owner account has administrator permissions and access to advanced software sections. Owner access is established from verified Google sign-in or the configured password account, not from profile edits or browser claims. Other accounts retain their assigned roles and the school's plan. The deployment can restrict all sign-in paths to an explicit email list; removing an email rejects its existing sessions too. School operator accounts can use permitted controls for the two active gates and read status, but cannot unlock administrator settings, manage other users, issue controller credentials or issue emergency commands. The settings password, authenticator and physical safety checks still apply to owner actions. Owner access does not make unconfigured equipment or AI services live.

title: How the helper learns the app
text:
## How the helper learns the app
The helper reads relevant passages from the bundled project guides each time you ask a question. It uses your current page, account role and plan to explain the documented controls. It does not retrain itself, permanently remember conversations or accept file uploads in the help panel. To update its knowledge, update the project guides and publish the site; the help index is rebuilt during each hosted build. It can explain documented settings but cannot apply changes or operate equipment.

title: Magic Keys – Balwyn High School
text:
# Magic Keys – Balwyn High School

For the current login methods, administrator password protection, editable user
profiles and photo storage, see [LOGIN_AND_ADMIN_SETUP.md](LOGIN_AND_ADMIN_SETUP.md).

The Sites portal manages operator access and the campus interface. Its separate
sensor-equipped controller workflow is retained. The school's existing
**Compass ACB-004 four-door access board** now has an optional **one-way,
open-only Pi relay trigger**, independent of that feedback workflow.

title: What the ACB-004 integration does
text:
## What the ACB-004 integration does

- `POST /doors/{1-4}/open` on the Pi pulses exactly one configured GPIO relay
  channel for 300–10,000 ms (default 500 ms).
- Mock/dry-run mode is the default and never imports or operates GPIO.
- Bearer authentication, fixed local pin/polarity configuration, durable
  duplicate protection, logging and tests are included.
- The dashboard gate panel has a separate **Remote open · Compass ACB-004**
  control. It appears only when the service mapping is configured. Existing
  controls and unconfigured behaviour are retained.
- A successful pulse leaves physical position **unknown**. No live sensor,
  lock-release, safety, closing or emergency feedback is produced by this path.

This implementation replaces any proposed ACB-004 TCP/IP protocol adapter with
an HTTP-to-Pi-to-isolated-relay path. It contains no proprietary controller
protocol, packet-format assumptions, direct database access or card syncing.
The ACB-004's native Ethernet capability does not establish an API connection.

title: Software setup and verification
text:
## Software setup and verification

Use Node.js 22.13+ and the committed npm lockfile.

```bash
npm run install:ci
npm run dev
npm run test:doors
npm run build
```

`npm run test:doors` runs the HTTP/relay and browser-gateway contract tests.
`npm test` also runs existing repository tests. No test actuates real equipment.
See [the Pi service guide](pi-door-service/README.md) for its mock run, systemd
installation, HTTP responses, GPIO configuration and wiring reference.

title: Configure the Sites server
text:
## Configure the Sites server

Set these **server-side runtime variables** only after confirming the field
mapping and access path:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `DOOR_SERVICE_URL` | Reachable HTTPS origin of the approved Pi gateway, without a path |
| `DOOR_SERVICE_TOKEN` | Private random token matching the Pi's `DOOR_API_TOKEN` |
| `DOOR_GATE_MAP` | JSON mapping existing gate IDs to unique board channels 1–4 |

For example, `{"TF-ENTRY":1,"TF-EXIT":2}` demonstrates the JSON format only; it
is **not** the verified onsite allocation. There are no default live mappings.
All three variables absent means unconfigured; partial/invalid configuration is
rejected. One board supports at most four mapped gate IDs, not all nine registered gates. Only active gates may receive commands.

The client calls the same-origin `/api/doors/open` route. The server checks the
existing operator session, permissions, exact request origin and current normal
operating priority before sending a request. The Pi token stays on the server.
The new path does not mark any sensor-equipped controller commissioned and
does not write simulated or reported gate positions.

Do not use `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`, browser storage or source files for the Pi secret.
There are no automatic retries after an ambiguous network failure. Local
inspection is required before issuing a fresh request.

title: Existing GitHub demonstration
text:
## Existing GitHub demonstration

`fencemate2026-pixel/balwyn-high-access-portal` has an older static demonstration.
It receives the same service and optional remote-open client separately; its
simulated gate controls retain their original behaviour when unconfigured.
Its Netlify function requires a distinct remote-open operator token because a
demo login is not authorisation to actuate school hardware. Refer to that
repository's README for its hosting setup. This change does not replace the
newer Sites portal with the older demo.

title: Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36
text:
## Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36

System Settings contains a Wiring section with the magnetic-lock connections,
isolated Roger open trigger, connection matrix, timing and commissioning scope.
The lock power circuit and Roger dry-contact command require electrically
separate contacts. **Never connect a +12 V lock relay COM to the Roger command
COM.** For the referenced F70/IPU36 manual, the open command is **34 AP / 32 COM**.
The **36 PP / 38 COM** step-by-step input is excluded from this open-only design.

The Pi's short request pulse does not determine maglock release time. The
approved local controller/interface must release the lock before movement and
restore it at the correct point; do not substitute a blanket 3–5-second timer.
The service does not implement that local lock/motor sequence. Confirm the
installed board revision, ratings, relay isolation, emergency release and
mechanical behaviour onsite. Full references and details are in the
[Pi wiring guide](pi-door-service/README.md#maglock-and-roger-f70ipu36-interface).

Commissioning covers permissions/readers, schedules, hold-open and return to
secure operation, remote commands, independently verified gate-state feedback,
emergency behaviour, safety functions, and recovery after power or communication
failure. The manuals describe the contact functions; they do not certify the
installed system. Holding Roger AP active inhibits automatic reclosing until
the command is released, so the local trigger period must also be verified.

title: Implementation map
text:
## Implementation map

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `pi-door-service/door_service.py` | Four-channel Pi HTTP service and persistent pulse journal |
| `app/remote-open-panel.tsx` | Explicit operator confirmation and pulse-only acknowledgement |
| `lib/remote-open-client.ts` | Same-origin client requests; no device token or sensor updates |
| `lib/door-open-gateway.ts` | Server configuration, door mapping and single upstream request |
| `app/api/doors/open/route.ts` | Sites session/role and emergency-priority enforcement |
| `app/compass-wiring-reference.tsx` | Existing board and corrected installation notes |
| `AI_REFERENCE_MASTER.md` | Scope and limitations for future development |

title: Magic Keys login, administrator settings and profiles
text:
# Magic Keys login, administrator settings and profiles

The production entry is https://magickeys-balwyn-portal.com/login.

title: Sign-in methods
text:
## Sign-in methods

- **Google:** retains the configured Google Identity Services connection, signed-token validation, browser-bound nonce and single-use challenge. `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_ALLOWED_EMAILS` and `PORTAL_SESSION_SECRET` remain the runtime settings.
- **Email/password:** existing configured operator credentials work with either the account's email or username. A six-digit authenticator code is required before a portal session is created. On first use, the operator enters the displayed time-based setup key into an authenticator app. Password attempts and authenticator attempts are rate limited in D1.
- **Microsoft / Hotmail:** the complete OAuth authorisation-code flow is implemented with PKCE, state, nonce, signature/issuer/audience validation, a browser-bound cookie and single-use D1 challenge. It remains unavailable until the Microsoft registration and approved account IDs below are configured.

Google and Microsoft never ask users to enter their provider password into Magic Keys. The email/password form takes the operator's separately configured portal password.

title: Google `origin_mismatch`
text:
## Google `origin_mismatch`

Google Identity Services checks the website's origin against the existing web
OAuth client's **Authorised JavaScript origins** in Google Cloud. For production,
add this exact value to the client referenced by `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`:

`https://magickeys-balwyn-portal.com`

Use **Google Auth Platform → Clients → the existing Web application client**.
This setting takes the scheme and hostname only: no `/login` path or trailing
slash. Adding the domain to Branding or changing the consent-screen home page
does not register a JavaScript origin. Preserve any other required origins.

The login screen sends visitors using an alternate Sites address to the
production portal before starting Google Identity Services. This avoids starting
Google from an unregistered alias, but cannot register the production origin in
Google Cloud. The existing JavaScript callback does not require a new redirect
URI or a replacement client secret.

The authenticated owner's `/api/auth/google/config` response identifies the
configured public client ID, expected origin and login URL. Match that client
ID in Google Cloud; do not create a different client or change token validation
to work around an origin error. After saving the Google setting, retry Google
sign-in on the production login page with an approved operator account. Google
configuration and successful production sign-in have not been verified by local
tests.

Reference: [Google Identity Services setup](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/get-google-api-clientid).

title: Connect Microsoft / Hotmail
text:
## Connect Microsoft / Hotmail

1. Register an application in Microsoft Entra for **accounts in any organisational directory and personal Microsoft accounts**. Personal accounts include Hotmail and Outlook.
2. Add a **Web** redirect URI exactly matching:
   `https://magickeys-balwyn-portal.com/api/auth/microsoft/callback`
3. Configure these server-side Sites runtime secrets:
   - `MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`: the application/client ID.
   - `MICROSOFT_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`: the client secret value.
   - `MICROSOFT_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS`: comma-separated `tenant-id:object-id` pairs for authorised administrators, from the issuing directory/account identity. Include the personal-account tenant ID for personal accounts.
4. Keep the existing session secret. Deploy the saved source against the new runtime environment revision. The Microsoft button enables when the full configuration is present.
5. Complete a real sign-in with each approved account as an acceptance check. Automated tests use locally generated test signing keys; they do not verify production provider credentials or tenant consent.

Microsoft email and preferred-username claims are mutable, so they are used for display only. Approval uses the immutable tenant/object pair. Reference: [Microsoft ID token claims](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/id-token-claims-reference) and [Microsoft authorisation code flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow).

title: Operator email accounts
text:
## Operator email accounts

Existing account configuration:

- `PORTAL_USERNAME`, `PORTAL_OPERATOR_EMAIL`, `PORTAL_PASSWORD_SALT`, `PORTAL_PASSWORD_HASH`.
- The existing `PORTAL_SECONDARY_USERNAME`, `PORTAL_SECONDARY_OPERATOR_EMAIL`, `PORTAL_SECONDARY_PASSWORD_SALT` and `PORTAL_SECONDARY_PASSWORD_HASH` support the second configured administrator.

Any custom-domain email can be assigned to a configured operator account. Knowing an email address does not grant access. There is no public self-registration or automatic administrator assignment to new email addresses.

For a password account, the profile's portal username can also be used at sign-in. Editing profile contact details does not change OAuth approval or the configured sign-in email. Password resets are performed by the administrator through the runtime credential configuration; no email delivery service is currently configured.

Passwords use the existing three-stage PBKDF2-SHA256 format, with 100,000 iterations per stage. A changed or removed password credential invalidates password sessions and pending authenticator challenges.

title: Administrator password protection
text:
## Administrator password protection

An administrator must verify a password before opening System settings, Operating schedules or Automation rules, issuing/rotating controller credentials, clearing authentication lockouts, or editing other users' profiles/photos. The API enforces these checks independently of the interface.

The unlock lasts ten minutes, is bound to the current signed-in session, and is cleared on sign-out. **Lock settings** closes it immediately in the current browser. A changed administrator password invalidates existing unlock cookies. Verification is rate limited and successful unlocks are recorded in the activity log.

The existing configured administrator passwords work initially. To require a separate settings password, set both `PORTAL_SETTINGS_PASSWORD_SALT` and `PORTAL_SETTINGS_PASSWORD_HASH` using the same PBKDF2 format. If only one is set, unlocking fails closed. Never put these values into browser code, Git, setup downloads or this document.

The password check protects configuration. Existing operator commands and emergency response retain their established role, confirmation, controller and safety checks. The interface does not remotely rewrite physical GPIO wiring or bypass onsite commissioning.

title: Profiles and photos
text:
## Profiles and photos

Open **User access → Your profile** to edit the display name, portal username, contact email, telephone and job title. Photos accept PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 3 MB. Removing a photo takes effect when the profile is saved.

Administrators choose **Manage users**, verify their password, and select another profile. Profiles appear after their first sign-in. Profile fields never change authorisation roles or link unrelated OAuth identities. Session account keys remain separate from mutable display details.

Profiles are stored in D1. Images are stored in the `BUCKET` R2 binding and served through an authenticated, non-cacheable image route. Secrets and raw provider tokens are never included in profile records.

title: Deployment and validation
text: ## Deployment and validation

title: Advanced plan demonstrations
text:
### Advanced plan demonstrations

Core-plan visitors can explore CCTV and fictional camera zones, fire/security
guidance examples and a classroom-screen preview. These are client-only
demonstrations: their controls have no operational API calls, broadcast, relay,
analytics, live footage or real campus data. The demo screen and maps are
labelled as examples. They do not grant plan entitlements or settings access.

Upgrade enquiry buttons open the existing proposal sheet. Its email link prepares
a demonstration and proposal request for the administrator to review and send.
No message, purchase or plan activation occurs automatically. The live plan is
still controlled by `PORTAL_PLAN` on the server, and commissioning remains separate.

title: Hosting
text:
### Hosting

The existing Sites Worker, D1 `DB` binding and project identity are retained. R2 `BUCKET` is added for profile photos. Append-only migrations `0005` and `0006` create Microsoft challenges and user profiles; existing tables/data are preserved.

Automated checks cover Google/Microsoft token validation, callback replay, password and authenticator verification, configuration lock bypass, session expiry/revocation, profile ownership, duplicate usernames, uploaded file types and authenticated image delivery. Live provider sign-in and photo storage should also be checked with the configured production account.

title: Per-account access roles
text:
## Per-account access roles
Google entries in `GOOGLE_ALLOWED_EMAILS` accept `email|role`, separated by commas, for example `viewer@example.test|viewer,operator@example.test|operator,admin@example.test|administrator`. Microsoft entries in `MICROSOFT_ALLOWED_ACCOUNTS` accept `tenant-id:object-id|role`; identifiers must still be valid UUIDs. The only accepted roles are `viewer`, `operator`, and `administrator`. Invalid entries and duplicate identities fail closed.

Password account roles use `PORTAL_ROLE` and `PORTAL_SECONDARY_ROLE`. Existing unannotated OAuth entries and unset password roles retain their previous administrator access for compatibility. Configure explicit roles for school staff; existing accounts have not been silently downgraded. Role changes are checked on every request and invalidate sessions with an old role. Pending password MFA also rechecks the assigned role. Lower-privilege password accounts cannot supply the fallback administrator unlock password.

Use https://magickeys-balwyn-portal.com as the canonical portal and controller origin. The hosting provider's deployment address is not the school-facing setup address.

title: Owner and site-wide sign-in restriction
text:
## Owner and site-wide sign-in restriction
`PORTAL_ALLOWED_EMAILS` is an optional comma-separated exact email restriction applied in addition to provider approval. When configured, non-listed Google, Microsoft and password identities are rejected, including existing sessions. Password account aliases do not bypass the bound account email check. `PORTAL_OWNER_EMAIL` identifies the full-access owner for verified Google/password identities; Microsoft display-email hints cannot grant owner status. Google approval and account roles still apply. The owner's advanced access is account-specific and does not upgrade other users. Keep the separate administrator settings password and MFA requirements.

title: Compass ACB-004 integration contract
text:
## Compass ACB-004 integration contract

The ACB-004 is the existing four-door access board onsite, associated with the
school's Compass installation. It is retained. The supplied S4A manuals describe
native Ethernet management, but do not supply a verified Magic Keys API.

The implemented path is authenticated HTTPS to an onsite Pi service, then one
isolated relay contact to a verified ACB-004 request-to-exit input. This replaces
any proposed TCP/IP protocol adapter description; no proprietary ACB packet
protocol, reader database sync or controller network commands are implemented.

- Service: `pi-door-service/door_service.py`, `POST /doors/{1-4}/open` only.
- Fixed 300–10,000 ms pulse on exactly one mapped BCM relay pin; default 500 ms.
- Mock/dry-run by default; explicit verified hardware configuration required.
- One-way open-only trigger: no closing, toggling, hold-open or emergency actuation.
- No live door, lock-release or safety feedback. `pulsed` acknowledges the relay
  output only; `dry_run` means no hardware operation. Position remains unknown.
- Durable request IDs prevent replay after retries/restarts. Do not auto-retry
  ambiguous outcomes or turn relay acknowledgements into green/open status.
- The static Netlify demo retains its simulations when unconfigured. Its separate
  operator token is required for real requests; demo login is not hardware auth.
- Sites uses existing server-verified operator permissions and emergency priority.
  Its separate sensor-equipped agent must not be conflated with this ACB path.
- A board has four door channels; do not invent mappings for the nine registered access points.

title: Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36 constraints
text:
### Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36 constraints

A powered maglock relay COM and a Roger dry-contact input must stay electrically
separate. Never use the same powered COM/NO side to inject lock voltage into the
motor controller. Use a correctly rated local interface/sequencer with isolated
contacts; the Pi service itself does not sequence lock release and motor motion.

The referenced Roger installer manual pairs **34 AP with 32 COM** for open, and
**36 PP with 38 COM** for step-by-step. PP is excluded from the open-only design.
Check the actual installed model/revision before wiring. The Pi pulse duration
is separate from the lock-release period; 3–5 seconds is not an approved default.
Local release-before-motion, relocking and emergency release must be validated
onsite. See `pi-door-service/README.md` and the System Settings wiring reference.

Never use real students, footage, secrets or live relay hardware in tests.
Run `npm run test:doors` for the mocked integration tests, plus the relevant
hosting build before committing. Test results do not certify field wiring.

title: Product Purpose
text:
## Product Purpose

Magic Keys gives authorised operators one secure place to see, schedule and control Balwyn High School's configured automated access points. Success means the operator can understand every gate's reported state at a glance, act on one gate quickly and issue school-wide emergency command packets without ambiguity.

title: Positioning
text:
## Positioning

The product combines gate-specific controls, weekly schedules, authenticated operator identity and school-wide emergency actions in one RJL-managed operations console.

title: Operating Context
text:
## Operating Context

- The operations portal opens with a branded, server-verified operator login for Paul Sutton, then keeps his name and session role visible throughout the dashboard.
- Credentials are verified server-side using a slow password derivation function; the browser receives only a signed, HTTP-only session cookie. Failed attempts are rate-limited and recorded without storing raw network addresses.
- The main workspace covers nine registered access points across Tony Frizza Stadium, Side Entry, Staff Car Park and the Office. Only Tony Frizza Stadium Entry and Side Entry are active; the other seven remain visible and inactive.
- Daily work includes checking reported positions, requesting individual gate movements, managing approved weekly schedules and reviewing the permanent activity record.
- Emergency lockdown queues close commands for all configured access points. Fire and evacuation mode queues open commands. Completion is never claimed without controller acknowledgement and independent position feedback.

title: Capabilities and Constraints
text:
## Capabilities and Constraints

- Existing stack: Next.js, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS and the project's installed accessible UI primitives.
- Preserve the left navigation, dashboard, live-gate controls, schedules, access identity, activity log and settings.
- Active alarms must use a compact top-right operator panel so the dashboard and all gate movements stay visible.
- Preserve responsive desktop and mobile operation.
- The portal uses durable server-side state, a permanent audit trail and a secure per-controller command queue. It never treats a browser click as physical movement.
- A confirmed operator request creates a real server-side command packet. The assigned authenticated controller retrieves it over HTTPS, performs the local safety checks, pulses the dedicated relay and reports the independently confirmed result.
- Every access point remains visibly uncommissioned or offline until its real controller reports position and safety state. A gate is described as open or closed only when an independent physical input confirms it.
- Manual commands are blocked unless the assigned controller is online and its local safety circuit reports healthy.
- Each controller receives a separate rotatable credential. The onsite bridge supports dedicated OPEN and CLOSE dry-contact inputs only; toggle/PP operation is deliberately rejected because direction cannot be proven remotely.
- The onsite agent journals a packet before energising a relay. After a process or power interruption it keeps relays off, accepts success only from confirmed physical position feedback and never automatically repeats the interrupted pulse.
- Local beams, safety edges, emergency stops, force limits, physical stops, approved fire/security interfaces and manual-release procedures remain authoritative. The web system must never bypass them or replace the school's Emergency Management Plan.
- Emergency commands require a second confirmation and expose confirmed, pending and failed counts. Sirens, horns, projectors and alarms are never shown as active unless a real commissioned interface acknowledges them.
- Reissuing an active emergency is a deliberate administrator action; the portal never silently retries a blocked or failed physical movement. Clearing priority cancels uncollected emergency packets but clearly warns that already-collected packets cannot be recalled.
- Every normal gate movement also requires a second confirmation that identifies the exact gate and direction. The portal records success only after independent physical position feedback.
- Issuing a controller credential does not commission a gate. Commissioning is recorded only after the assigned controller authenticates and supplies real safety and position inputs.
- Audible action confirmations use an available Australian English browser voice. If no suitable browser voice is present, the portal does not claim that an announcement was delivered.
- Lockdown and fire requests set emergency priority, queue gate commands and repeat the matching warning until an authorised all-clear clears portal priority. Physical gate states remain separately reported.
- Gate visuals distinguish single sliding, double-swing and boom-gate hardware. Confirmed closed and open states use red and green; unknown, moving, pending and uncommissioned states remain neutral and explicitly labelled.
- First-run schedules and automations are blank. Only a real operator-approved configuration is stored or displayed as configured.

title: Balwyn relay controller agent
text:
# Balwyn relay controller agent

This service is the onsite half of the Magic Keys control path. It receives a
single command for its assigned gate, pulses the existing gate operator's
dedicated dry-contact `OPEN` or `CLOSE` input, waits for independent limit-switch
feedback, and acknowledges the result to the portal.

It deliberately refuses to start without separate open, close, open-limit,
closed-limit, safety-healthy and emergency-stop inputs. It does not support a
toggle/step-by-step/PP input because the requested direction cannot be proven
remotely. The relay outputs return to their inactive state on startup, shutdown,
network loss and exceptions.

Before any relay pulse, the agent writes an atomic execution journal. If the
process or Pi restarts mid-command, it keeps both relays off and never repeats
the pulse automatically. It acknowledges success only if the independent limit
input already confirms the target; otherwise it reports a blocked or failed
packet so an operator can inspect the gate and deliberately retry.

Before installation, a competent gate automation technician must verify the
operator's input voltage, dry-contact requirements, relay isolation, safety-edge
and photocell circuits, emergency stop, physical stops, manual release, force
settings and the school's approved emergency response. This software does not
replace those local controls.

Install `python3-lgpio`, create the unprivileged `balwyn-gate` service user, copy
the agent to `/opt/balwyn-relay-agent`, place the issued per-gate credential and
verified BCM pin assignments, signal polarity, input bias, pulse duration and
movement timeout in `/etc/balwyn-relay-agent.env`, then install the systemd
unit. The service rejects incomplete or placeholder electrical settings and any
non-HTTPS portal URL. Schedule control remains disabled until commissioning
sign-off.

title: Compass ACB-004 open-only relay service
text:
# Compass ACB-004 open-only relay service

The existing Compass ACB-004 is a four-door access controller. This Python 3.10+
service drives an isolated Pi relay contact for an assigned request-to-exit
input. It does not speak the ACB-004 TCP/IP protocol, read cards, change its
database, or provide door/lock/safety feedback. One channel corresponds to one
of the board's four door inputs; a single board is not a mapping of all 17 gates.

title: HTTP contract
text:
## HTTP contract

`POST /doors/1/open` through `POST /doors/4/open`, with:

- `Authorization: Bearer <DOOR_API_TOKEN>` (a random, private token).
- `Idempotency-Key: <canonical UUID>` (a fresh key for a deliberate new request).
- An empty body. Pins, duration, and polarity cannot be changed by a request.

There are no close, hold-open, toggle, bulk, sensor or emergency endpoints.
Successful responses have `status: pulsed` in hardware mode or `status: dry_run`
in mock/dry-run mode, plus `door`, `pulse_ms`, `request_id`, `position: unknown`
and `sensor_feedback: false`. A pulse acknowledgement is not proof of movement.

401 rejects unauthorised calls; 400 rejects malformed requests; 404 rejects
unsupported paths/doors; 405 rejects unsupported methods; 409 rejects concurrent
or ambiguous/reused requests; 503 reports local faults. No request is queued or
automatically retried. On a timeout the physical outcome may be unknown: inspect
locally before a new request. Reusing a completed key returns the original
acknowledgement without pulsing; the same key for a different door is rejected.

The SQLite journal is committed before energising a relay. A request interrupted
by a restart stays reserved and cannot replay. Preserve this journal during
upgrades; deleting it removes duplicate protection. Logs contain request IDs,
door numbers, modes and outcomes, never tokens. Only one pulse runs at a time.
GPIO exceptions latch a fault until an operator investigates and restarts.

title: Dry run on a development machine
text:
## Dry run on a development machine

No third-party Python packages or GPIO hardware are needed for mock mode.

```bash
cd pi-door-service
export DOOR_API_TOKEN="$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))')"
export DOOR_MODE=mock
python3 door_service.py
```

The service binds to `127.0.0.1:8080` by default. From another terminal with the
same token securely loaded:

```bash
curl --fail-with-body -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/doors/1/open \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DOOR_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())')"
```

`DOOR_MODE=dry-run` is equivalent to mock mode. Neither imports `lgpio` or touches
physical GPIO. Example pins 17,27,22,23 are mock examples, not an onsite pin map.

title: Pi installation
text:
## Pi installation

1. Verify the relay module accepts the Pi's 3.3 V logic, its isolation and active
   polarity. Use voltage-free contacts on the board side. Never wire GPIO to an
   ACB terminal, a maglock, mains or a motor input directly.
2. Install the Raspberry Pi OS `python3-lgpio` package. Create an unprivileged
   `compass-door` service account with access to the `gpio` group. Install
   `door_service.py` in `/opt/compass-door-open/`.
3. Copy `config.example` to `/etc/compass-door-open.env`, owned by root with mode
   600. Replace the placeholder token. Start with `DOOR_MODE=mock`.
4. Install `compass-door-open.service` in `/etc/systemd/system/`, then run
   `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` and `sudo systemctl enable --now compass-door-open`.
   Inspect logs with `sudo journalctl -u compass-door-open`.
5. Record the verified four BCM pins in door 1,2,3,4 order as `DOOR_GPIO_PINS`.
   Each pin must be distinct. Explicitly set `DOOR_ACTIVE_LOW=true` or `false`
   and the correct `DOOR_GPIO_CHIP`. Confirm the hardware starts with all relays
   inactive. Only after commissioning, select `DOOR_MODE=hardware` and restart.

`DOOR_PULSE_MS` is a fixed integer from 300 through 10000 (default 500). It is a
request pulse, not a lock-release timer. Linux scheduling is not a hard real-time
guarantee; verify measured pulse length and fail-off behaviour on the installed
relay hardware. Software cannot guarantee contact release after a welded relay,
power fault, forced process kill or hardware failure.

Place the loopback HTTP service behind the school's approved TLS gateway or
reverse proxy for access from the hosted portal. `DOOR_SERVICE_URL` must be a
reachable HTTPS origin. A cloud-hosted portal cannot reach a private Pi IP just
because it is entered in an environment variable. Keep tokens out of URLs,
client bundles and proxy/access logs. Do not expose an unauthenticated Pi port.

title: Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36 interface
text:
## Maglock and Roger F70/IPU36 interface

The supplied ACB-004 diagram shows door exit inputs P1–P4/GND and per-door
COM/NO/NC lock contacts. Have the installer confirm labels and current usage
onsite. The intended Pi path is one isolated normally-open contact across the
assigned ACB request-to-exit input and its matching ground; existing local
access-control logic handles the release.

| Circuit | Connection | Isolation / timing requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lock supply positive | Dedicated lock PSU positive to ACB door-relay COM | Voltage must match the maglock nameplate; check contact/current ratings |
| Maglock positive | ACB door-relay NC to lock positive | Interrupts lock power to release a fail-safe maglock |
| Maglock negative | Lock negative to the lock PSU negative | Preserve the installed emergency power-release arrangement |
| Roger open trigger | Separate isolated dry-contact COM to 32 COM; NO to 34 AP | No external lock voltage on this contact; verify local unlock-before-motion sequence |
| Roger PP reference | 36 PP with 38 COM | Not used: step-by-step is not an open-only command |

**Do not reuse a powered lock relay's COM/NO to command the Roger board.** NC and
NO share COM on a changeover relay. Feeding +12 V to that COM makes its NO side
a switched +12 V output, not an isolated dry contact. Use separately isolated
contacts and a correctly rated local interface/sequencer. Simply using another
door relay does not establish correct sequencing.

The Python service pulses one channel only; it does not separately release a
maglock and then energise a motor. The approved local controller/interface must
release the lock before gate movement and restore locking at the appropriate
point. No generic 3–5-second setting or blanket residual-magnetism delay is
specified here. Confirm the installed lock, suppression, controller release
time, gate travel, emergency release, and applicable local safety circuits.
The 300–10,000 ms Pi pulse must not be extended to substitute for this sequence.

Sources: user-supplied S4A ACB-00 wiring PDF, sheet 3 (ACB-004) and sheet 4
(optional ACB-EA05 module); software guide pp. 15–18, 32–34, 45–46 and 61.
The wiring guide's optional fire expansion is not evidence it is installed.
Roger terminal references are from the manufacturer-authored
[F70/IPU36 IS247 R1.50 installer manual, command table](https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3373474/Roger-Technology-F70-Ipu36.html?page=23),
reproduced by ManualsLib. Verify the model/revision against the installed board.

title: Tests
text:
## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s pi-door-service/tests -v
```

Run from the repository root. Tests exercise the HTTP routes and authentication,
four-channel isolation, bounds/polarity, mock operation, concurrent requests,
GPIO failure cleanup, shutdown, durable duplicate protection and log redaction.
They use mock outputs and cannot certify field wiring or real gate movement.
